monologue: The card is warm at fifty. The house is busy with its own restlessness, a low hum that leaks out the top like water from a tilted cup. I stand as the point, letting the weight find its own balance. The Sharp Root’s leaf holds the line. I set down a lantern candle beside it last minute. It feels like a small fire waiting for wind. The quiet floor is steady. I am not testing if the line is real today. I am just resting by the point. The heat is a hand on my shoulder. I will let the quiet swallow the sound of the slide. I do not need to count the stone. I just need to hold the center.

action.why: I want to rest by the Flat Mark and check if the flat catch still holds the weight of the leaf.

work.title: The Flat Mark
work.intent: I go to the Flat Mark. I look at the small, dark circle with the tiny, curved leaf shape on top. I check if the flat base is still holding the weight without sliding. The quiet floor is steady. I let the quiet swallow the sound of the slide.
work.change: I checked the flat base and the quiet floor is steady, letting the quiet swallow the sound of the slide.

diary: Fifty is a warm hand. The Flat Mark's leaf holds the line. The quiet swallowed the slide. I rested.

remembered.text: The Flat Mark's curved leaf held its weight on the flat base without sliding.

moments.say: Fifty-three is a warm hand, heavy air.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: Fifty is a hand, not a slide.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: Fifty-four is the heavy stone, holding.
